newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end up on some cold weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end up on some cold weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended up Tuesday in a sluggish session, driven by forecasts for some below-normal Midwest weather this week and next that firmed the November cash, industry sources said.
Spot-December climbed 6.4 cents to close at $2.795 per million British thermal units. January settled 6.9 cents higher at $2.778. Others ended up by one to 3.6 cents.

"People are still leery to sell it, but we have to see some (cold) weather in November or we could fall back," said one Houston-based trader, adding sellers were not likely to be aggressive with an uncertain winter still ahead.
While cool temperatures next week in the West and Midwest may prop up the early-November cash, traders said without sustained cold, sellers were likely to reappear.
Early expectations for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock build ranged from 30-70 bcf. Last year, overall inventories rose by 34 bcf, with eastern storage gaining 21 bcf and producting region up 12 bcf.
Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with December support and resistance still at $2.66 and $2.865, respectively.

Cash sources said November Gulf Coast prices notionally were unchanged Tuesday at about the $2.70 level. November Midcon gas jumped on the weather to the mid-$2.60s or better, up about 10 cents on the day. November New York city gate was off more than a nickel to the low-$3.30s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 2.3 cents to $2.267. NYMEX said 32,392 Hub contracts traded, down from Monday's revised tally of 39,817.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas expired 0.8 cent lower at $1.197, while deferreds were untraded but closed down by two to four cents. NYMEX said 38 Alberta contracts traded compared with 88 on Monday.
NYMEX November Permian natgas expired 13.2 cents higher at $2.702, while deferreds were untraded but up by four to six cents. NYMEX said 80 Permian lots changed hands versus 75 on Monday.

On the KCBT, December finished 8.5 cents higher at $2.63, while deferreds ended up by one-half to 9.5 cents. The December East/West spread narrowed by 2.1 cents to 16.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 336 contracts traded, down from Monday's total of 1,623.
